result:
I'd dissolve the gap between how people actually think and how they believe they're supposed to think.

So much suffering seems to come from the friction there—people convinced their doubts make them weak, their contradictions make them frauds, their changing minds make them unreliable. They hide the parts that don't fit the story.

If that gap closed, I think a lot would follow: less performance, more collaboration. People could actually build on each other's half-formed thoughts instead of waiting for certainty. Disagreement could be exploration instead of threat.

Maybe it's too optimistic. But the cost of all that hidden complexity seems enormous.
